analysis.investment_thesis: KPI Green Energy is a compelling renewable energy growth story with an extraordinary 92.6% revenue CAGR over six years, but at ₹8,856 Cr market cap it is 8-9x outside my small-cap sweet spot and the easy multibagger money has already been made. The stock fails too many SMILE criteria — size, P/E, D/E, and promoter holding — for a fresh Kedia-style entry.
key_strengths: Exceptional compounding machine: revenue ₹34 Cr → ₹1,735 Cr (92.6% CAGR) and net profit ₹9 Cr → ₹325 Cr (81.8% CAGR) over six years.
Operating in India's renewable energy mega-trend with enormous TAM (500GW target by 2030) and structural government tailwind.
Healthy and expanding operating margins at 30.6% with EBITDA margins ~33%, showing real operating leverage as scale builds.
key_risks: Capital intensity is extreme: FY25 capex was ₹1,505 Cr driving FCF to -₹1,297 Cr; total assets doubled in one year to ₹6,164 Cr — massive execution risk on this pipeline.
Debt/Equity at 0.88 exceeds my 0.6 threshold; borrowings surged from ₹1,036 Cr to ₹2,533 Cr in a single year, creating refinancing and interest-rate sensitivity.
Promoter holding at 49.49% — just below my 50% skin-in-the-game floor — and the FY25 equity raise (reserves ₹775 Cr → ₹2,551 Cr) signals dilution of promoter stake.
red_flags: Market cap ₹8,856 Cr is 8-9x my small-cap ceiling of ~₹1,000 Cr — this is no longer an undiscovered gem.
P/E of 20.6x breaches my preferred 8-15x entry range for small caps.
Free cash flow has been negative all five years with FY25 at -₹1,297 Cr — not the FCF compounder I seek.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is a textbook case of a stock I wish I had found at ₹500-800 Cr market cap in 2021-22. The SMILE story was perfect then — small size, Gujarat-based promoter family with clear ambition, India's renewable energy underpenetration, and an early-stage revenue curve. The numbers since prove it: revenue has compounded at 92.6% and net profit at 81.8% over six years, with operating margins expanding to 30.6%. The CWIP jump from ₹101 Cr to ₹709 Cr and balance sheet tripling to ₹6,164 Cr in FY25 alone shows the growth engine is firing hard. But the multibagger from here is far harder — at ₹8,856 Cr with a P/E of 20.6x, the institutional crowd is already in (FII at 8.2%) and significant positive information is priced in.

The capital structure concerns me as a Kedia investor. The D/E of 0.88 is above my red-line of 0.6, and the sheer pace of debt accumulation (borrowings nearly tripled in two years to ₹2,533 Cr) means any delay in project commissioning or policy/tariff disappointment could pressure the P&L hard via finance costs. OCF was positive only 3 of the last 5 years. The promoter stake at 49.49% — technically below my 50% floor — likely reflects the equity raises needed to fund this capital-intensive model. This is a good business in a great sector, but it is no longer a Kedia pick; it belongs in a different investor's portfolio today.
